name: 149 Medical
description: 149 Medical is dedicated to improving outcomes for premature infants through innovative, life-changing technology. Primary focus: reducing morbidity and mortality by providing continuous, real-time monitoring of cerebral blood flow to detect and mitigate risks such as ventricular hemorrhage. Flagship device: NIRDS1, a non-invasive intracranial blood flow sensor validated in over 1,000 children, currently in clinical evaluation, licensed exclusively from Massachusetts General Hospital.
products: Continuous non-invasive cerebral blood flow monitor (clinical prototype) — clinical-stage, non-invasive optical monitoring system for real-time cerebral blood flow measurement in premature infants; early warning of intraventricular hemorrhage risk
expertise_areas: Neonatal clinical monitoring and NICU study conduct
Clinical validation and comparative physiological testing
Regulatory affairs and quality systems for medical devices
Signal processing and algorithm development for physiological signals
key_technologies: Laser speckle / speckle contrast optical sensing
Real-time signal processing and blood flow estimation algorithms
publications: Validation of Diffuse Correlation Spectroscopy Measures of Critical Closing Pressure against Transcranial Doppler Ultrasound in Stroke Patients (Wu et al., 2021)
Validation of DCS against 15O-water PET for Regional Cerebral Blood Flow Measurement in Neonatal Piglets (Giovanella et al., 2020)
Cerebral Hemodynamics in Preterm Infants During Positional Intervention (Buckley et al., 2009)

expected_scores.notes: Strong operational medicine (environmental/physiologic monitoring) and clinical rehab fit. Civilian NICU market is the dual-use proof. Not a combat trauma play — hemorrhage here is intracranial, not battlefield. Low infectious disease relevance. Good example of a company that scores well on operational medicine but would be missed by a hemorrhage-keyword search.
